Estoy desarrollando un explorador person:
I'm developing a personal explorer of cultural associations: text, images, music, and memories connected through graded relationships and human review.

The experience I want to study is specific: start with an idea, find a file, and discover a path that helps you listen, compare, or write something new.

An LLM proposes concepts and associations; users review its interpretation. Vectors retrieve candidates, and the graph enables connection exploration. Optional synthesis proposes a reading of the results.

An analysis of 50 exported paths identifies 107 distinct assets across texts, audio, and images. These are case studies, not a benchmark or a measure of the entire graph. One case connects two songs through themes of isolation, identity, and digital criticism: an invitation to compare them, not a causal explanation.

The analysis also changed how I present the system. Weights are not calibrated confidence; source-level privacy needs to be completed during synthesis; and a compelling narrative must be checked against its originals.

The next proposed experiment will compare lexical, vector, and hybrid retrieval with graph expansion under the same budget. I want to measure relevance, support, and useful discoveries, alongside the cost of human review.

This is an original implementation focused on personal cultural curation. Scientific novelty and improvement over other methods remain open questions.
